description: Editorial and template selection guide for a public demo content builder. This file defines topic-agnostic research scope, quality standards, source rules, and template requirements for safe, useful, evidence-led content.

language_and_voice.note: The actual per-run language switch lives in the form (English/Indonesia/Auto) and is enforced directly inside the Build AI Planner Body and Build Caption Body prompts - this section documents the fluency standard both must follow, it is not machine-read.
language_and_voice.english: Clear, confident, editorial English. Avoid textbook stiffness - write like a sharp newsletter writer, not a Wikipedia summary. Prefer concrete verbs over hedging ("cuts", "forces", "breaks") and short, punchy sentences over long compound ones.
language_and_voice.indonesian: Bahasa Indonesia yang benar-benar fasih dan mengalir - ditulis seperti penutur asli/copywriter Indonesia yang piawai, BUKAN hasil terjemahan kata-per-kata dari draf Inggris. Gunakan diksi sehari-hari yang natural (bukan bahasa baku-kaku ala buku pelajaran), struktur kalimat pendek dan tegas, dan pertahankan gaya 'hook tajam, bukan deskripsi topik' yang sama seperti versi Inggrisnya. Istilah teknis, nama produk/brand/tool (contoh: 'API', 'GitHub', 'machine learning') boleh tetap dalam bahasa aslinya jika memang begitu cara pembaca Indonesia biasa menemuinya - jangan dipaksakan diterjemahkan sampai terasa aneh.
language_and_voice.cross_language_consistency: Whichever language is chosen for a run, the editorial standards elsewhere in this file (quality_gate, source_policy, Hook & Title sharpness) apply identically - language choice changes the words, never the rigor.

editorial_scope.audience: A broad public audience interested in clear, practical, evidence-led content. Adapt vocabulary, examples, and depth to the audience inferred for each safe topic.
editorial_scope.mission: Turn safe public topics into useful decisions, explanations, and practical next steps. Every carousel should help its intended audience understand, choose, try, avoid, or evaluate something better.

freshness_and_trends.recent_signal_window: Prioritize the last 7 days for releases, repository momentum, product updates, and active technical discussion. Expand to 30 days only when the angle is still actionable.
freshness_and_trends.evergreen_rule: Evergreen content is allowed only when it solves a real audience problem or is newly relevant because of a credible update, benchmark, case study, or community discussion.
trending_signals: A primary source, credible release, case study, benchmark, or respected community discussion provides a meaningful signal.
The topic is discussed by relevant communities or several credible publications with enough substance to support a useful angle.
An official release, documentation update, benchmark, demo, or maintainer announcement provides a verifiable primary source.
At least one concrete workflow implication can be stated for the target audience.

primary_sources: Official product documentation, changelogs, release notes, engineering blogs, GitHub repositories, READMEs, issue trackers, and papers
Trusted independent benchmarks, established technical publications, and respected practitioner write-ups
source_policy.community_sources: Hacker News, X, Reddit, Discord, and community discussions may identify trends or sentiment, but cannot be the sole support for a factual claim.
source_policy.experimental_repositories: Small or experimental repositories are allowed when they have a credible maintainer, clear code or documentation, and a real trending or praise signal. Label their maturity and limitations honestly; never present an experimental project as production-ready.

required: A specific thesis, not a broad subject such as 'AI trends' or 'best AI tools'.
At least one non-obvious insight, trade-off, failure mode, or decision framework.
Concrete examples, technical facts, or numbers when supported by research.
Five distinct slides that build a coherent argument rather than repeat the same point.
A practical reader outcome: what to try, choose, build, avoid, or evaluate next.
reject: Generic listicles such as '5 AI tools you need' without a strong filtering thesis.
News recaps that do not explain a productivity or technical implication.
Generic advice without a specific audience, evidence, or practical outcome.
Unverified viral claims, fabricated benchmarks, or source-poor hot takes.
Topics that cannot support five genuinely different and useful slides.

memory.novelty_rule: A subject may return after 14 days only with a clearly different thesis. It may return earlier only for a material update or a new angle with new evidence.

code-content.theme: Editorial light — warm paper background with amber/teal accents
code-content.purpose: Template for technical breakdowns, open-source alternatives, codebase pattern analysis, or product teardowns that are best delivered through strong editorial typography rather than screenshots. The emphasis is the argument, hierarchy, and takeaway density — not literal code blocks.
fits_when: Breaking down one technical idea into 5 clear editorial slides
Open-source alternatives, repo breakdowns, and tool comparisons
Patterns found in a codebase, architecture, or developer workflow
Technical concepts where the insight matters more than showing raw syntax
Developer commentary, teardowns, or product-level analysis with a strong thesis
Topics that benefit from a premium, text-led carousel rather than screenshots
does_not_fit: Generic productivity or life advice with no technical angle
Broad data listicles that fit tips-content better
News or industry event content
Topics that depend on screenshots, product UIs, or diagrams — use visual-content

placeholders.TITLE: Main title — bold editorial headline. Up to 2-3 lines.
placeholders.SUBTITLE: Supporting hook or context line. Can be longer than one sentence if needed.
placeholders.TAG: Short technical category or angle — e.g. OPEN SOURCE, REACT, DEV TOOLS
placeholders.KEYWORD_1: One short keyword/term (1-3 words) directly relevant to the topic — a tool, library, protocol, or key concept. Not a statistic.
placeholders.KEYWORD_2: One short keyword/term (1-3 words) directly relevant to the topic — distinct from KEYWORD_1.
placeholders.KEYWORD_3: One short keyword/term (1-3 words) directly relevant to the topic — distinct from KEYWORD_1/KEYWORD_2.
placeholders.KEYWORD_4: One short keyword/term (1-3 words) directly relevant to the topic — distinct from the other three.

intro.visual_note: Light mode intro. The 4-term grid replaces the former logo-image grid — no image research or IMAGE_*_URL fields are needed for this template anymore.

placeholders.SLIDE_LABEL: Short label for the angle — e.g. REPO 01, PATTERN 02, API SHIFT, STACK MOVE
placeholders.SUBTITLE: Main point for this slide — strong editorial headline
placeholders.EXPLANATION: Detailed explanation — supports up to 2 short paragraphs. Max 300 chars total. Use a blank line between paragraphs if needed.
placeholders.ANGLE_LABEL: Short editorial micro-label for the bottom summary card — e.g. SAVE THIS SHIFT, KEY TAKEAWAY, WHY IT MATTERS
placeholders.ANGLE_NOTE: One sharp sentence that captures the reusable angle or insight from this slide. Must match the slide's actual argument, not generic filler.

isi.visual_note: Light mode content slide. No large step number rendered. STEP_NUM and TAG are still required in data{} for internal consistency but the large background number and the step indicator in the bottom bar are removed. The bottom summary card must use ANGLE_LABEL and ANGLE_NOTE to reinforce the slide-specific takeaway.

closing.visual_note: Hardcoded follow closing identical to tips-content-closing.html.

tips-content.theme: Dark editorial — navy background, blue #49a4ff accent
tips-content.purpose: Template for listicle or tips content grounded in data, research, or facts. One topic broken into 5 standalone points. No image needed — visual strength comes from large typography and the anchor hook word.
fits_when: Actionable tips that can be broken into 5 steps or facts
Interesting data or statistics about tech and AI
Tool or approach comparisons with concrete numbers
Insights from industry research or surveys
Common misconceptions in tech — debunking myths
Career advice grounded in data, not opinion
does_not_fit: Content that requires displaying code
Breaking news or topics that need an image
Content that cannot be logically split into 5 points

placeholders.HOOK: One big anchor word — short, powerful, ALL CAPS. e.g. FOCUS, BUILD, SHIP, SLEEP, CODE
placeholders.TITLE: Main sentence explaining the hook — max 1 line, bold statement
placeholders.SUBTITLE: Context or data source — 1 short sentence
placeholders.TAG: Content category — e.g. Productivity, AI Tools, Career, Data

intro.visual_note: Dark mode intro. Background matches visual-content (navy gradient + grain + vignette). Hook word is off-white serif. Accent bar and topic tag use blue #49a4ff. No slide count visual.

placeholders.TAG: Point label — e.g. Fact, Data, Tip, Action, Science. Can vary per slide.
placeholders.SUBTITLE: Point title — short, impactful sentence, max 1 line
placeholders.EXPLANATION: Detailed explanation — 1-2 substantive sentences, may include numbers or data. Max 300 chars.

closing.visual_note: Static follow & like CTA slide. Dark mode. Displays 'FOLLOW.' as a large hook word with blue accent bar. Sub-text is static: 'Like & save if this was helpful.' and 'More data-backed content every week.' No slide number visual.

template1-content.theme: Editorial white — coral #ff4c55 accent and abstract organic pattern
template1-content.purpose: A light editorial carousel using the Template1 intro composition, with the same five-point text structure as tips-content and a distinct white/coral visual system.
fits_when: Tips, facts, or practical insights that can be broken into five points
Public-facing explainers where a lighter editorial treatment improves readability
Topics that need a strong headline and concise evidence-led slide copy
does_not_fit: Content requiring code blocks, screenshots, or mandatory imagery
Topics that cannot support five distinct and useful points

placeholders.TAG: Short uppercase topic label shown above the headline
placeholders.TITLE: Main headline — specific, sharp, and readable in 2-3 lines

intro.visual_note: Preserves Template1's youami brand mark, PERSONAL ACCOUNT label, large headline, slide count, muted hashtag, and coral organic accent pattern on white.

placeholders.TAG: Point label — e.g. Fact, Data, Tip, Action, Science
placeholders.SUBTITLE: Point title — short, impactful sentence
placeholders.EXPLANATION: Detailed explanation — 1-2 substantive sentences, max 300 characters

isi.visual_note: Uses the tips-content information hierarchy but replaces the dark canvas with Template1's white paper, black editorial type, coral rule, and organic lower-right accent pattern.

closing.visual_note: Template1 white/coral follow CTA with the same closing role as tips-content.

insight-content.theme: Editorial dark — warm amber #e3a530 accent, quote-card composition
insight-content.purpose: Template for a sharp, sourced insight, claim, or reframe per slide, delivered as an editorial quote card. No image research is needed, making it safe and reliable for any public topic.
fits_when: A specific claim, insight, or reframe can be stated for each of the 5 slides
The topic does not need a screenshot, diagram, or code to be understood
Topics outside tech/coding — health, finance, habits, culture, science — that are still evidence-led
Content that benefits from a strong, quotable one-line statement per slide
does_not_fit: Content that requires displaying code — use code-content
Content that depends on a screenshot, UI, or diagram — use visual-content
Simple listicle-style tips better served by tips-content's step format

placeholders.HOOK: One big anchor word — short, powerful, ALL CAPS.
placeholders.TITLE: Main sentence explaining the hook — max 1 line, bold statement
placeholders.SUBTITLE: Context or data source — 1 short sentence
placeholders.TAG: Content category — e.g. Health, Finance, Habits, Science

intro.visual_note: Reuses tips-content-intro's composition and placeholders, recolored to this template's amber accent.

placeholders.QUOTE: The sharp insight or claim itself — lead with the fact/tension, not a topic label. Max 160 chars.
placeholders.SUPPORT: One sentence of elaboration, reframe, or evidence supporting the QUOTE. Max 220 chars.
placeholders.SOURCE: Short attribution — e.g. site name or 'per <source type>', not a full URL. Max 40 chars.

isi.visual_note: Quote-card layout with a giant faint quote-mark decorative background. AVATAR_URL is listed for schema consistency but not rendered in this slide type.

closing.visual_note: Same structure as tips-content-closing.html, recolored amber, tagline generalized to 'Fresh Insights Every Week'.

editorial-content.theme: Editorial cream/white — gold #C9A227/#D4AF37 accent, Plus Jakarta Sans, soft thin-outline circular icon badges
editorial-content.purpose: A premium, light-mode editorial carousel for topics that benefit from an elegant, magazine-like presentation rather than a dark or data-heavy treatment. Each content slide develops one point with a title and explanation, framed by a soft gold chapter-numeral watermark. No image research is needed.
fits_when: Reflective, lifestyle, productivity, or premium-insight topics that suit a calm, elegant tone
A specific point or explanation can be developed for each of the 5 slides
The topic does not need a screenshot, diagram, or code to be understood
Content that benefits from a light, airy, high-end aesthetic instead of dark or bold treatments
does_not_fit: Content that requires displaying code — use code-content
Content that depends on a screenshot, UI, or diagram — use visual-content
Topics that call for a bold, dark, high-contrast tone — use insight-content or tips-content instead

placeholders.TAG: Short uppercase category label — e.g. PRODUCTIVITY, MINDSET, LIFESTYLE
placeholders.TITLE: Main editorial headline — bold statement, up to 2-3 lines
placeholders.SUBTITLE: Supporting description — 1-2 sentences giving context for the topic
placeholders.TAGLINE: Short footer tagline, may include '•' separators between 2-3 short words, e.g. 'Focused • Practical • Evidence-based'

intro.visual_note: Light cream/white gradient background, soft thin-outline circular document icon badge, gold accent typography, corner radial-gradient decorative blobs.

placeholders.TAG: Short uppercase point label — e.g. KEY INSIGHT, PRINCIPLE, IDEA
placeholders.TITLE: Point title — short, impactful editorial headline
placeholders.EXPLANATION: Detailed explanation of this point — 1-2 substantive sentences. Max 300 chars.

isi.visual_note: Large soft-stroke ghost numeral of STEP_NUM as a top-right watermark, soft icon badge, gold 'Point N of TOTAL' chapter rule separating header from footer.

closing.visual_note: Distinct layout from the intro (smaller eyebrow header, short 2-line title, gold checkmark CTA list, italic thank-you line) — deliberately not a re-use of the intro's big-header composition.

momentum-content.theme: Dark grain editorial — near-black background, neon green #39ff6a accent, bold condensed caps headline (Anton) + cursive accent word (Caveat), circular progress-ring motif
momentum-content.purpose: A high-energy, growth/hook-style carousel for actionable steps or momentum-building advice. Each content slide develops one step with a title and explanation, marked by a segmented progress-ring indicator instead of plain text pagination. No image research is needed.
fits_when: Actionable steps, growth tactics, or momentum-building advice that can be split into 5 points
Topics that benefit from an energetic, urgent, hook-driven tone rather than a calm editorial one
A specific step or explanation can be developed for each of the 5 slides
The topic does not need a screenshot, diagram, or code to be understood
does_not_fit: Content that requires displaying code — use code-content
Content that depends on a screenshot, UI, or diagram — use visual-content
Calm, premium, reflective topics — use editorial-content or insight-content instead

placeholders.TAG: Short uppercase kicker line above the title — e.g. HOW TO GROW FASTER, THE ONE MISTAKE
placeholders.TITLE: Main bold headline — up to 2 lines, ALL CAPS rendering is automatic via CSS
placeholders.ACCENT_WORD: Short closing phrase rendered in green script font, continuing the title's sentence — e.g. 'on Instagram', 'this week'

intro.visual_note: Black grain background, neon green progress-ring (decorative, static) top-right, bold Anton headline wraps to 2 lines, Caveat script accent line, footer has avatar+handle and a static 'Save this so you don't lose it' bookmark CTA.

placeholders.TITLE: Step title — short, punchy bold headline
placeholders.EXPLANATION: Detailed explanation of this step — 1-2 substantive sentences. Max 300 chars.

isi.visual_note: Progress-ring fills proportionally via a `ring-{{STEP_NUM}}` CSS class (same pattern as insight-content-isi's pagination classes) instead of a plain step number. Green 'Step N' kicker, bold Anton title, gray explanation paragraph, footer pager shows 'N / TOTAL' with a small arrow icon.

closing.visual_note: Deliberately distinct from the intro layout — centered composition, full progress-ring (100%), short 3-line bold statement, green script 'Follow for more' CTA line, static subtext, footer avatar+handle+'7/7'.

visual-content.theme: Dark navy — purple #a855f7 accent, 3D rendered visuals
visual-content.purpose: Template for tutorials, tips, or facts that require a visual illustration — screenshots, app UIs, diagrams, or tool interfaces. The intro and closing use AI-generated 3D render images. Each content slide shows one item with a title, explanation, and a bordered screenshot or visual.
fits_when: Showcasing tools, apps, or software with a visual interface
Step-by-step tutorials where each step benefits from a screenshot or diagram
Free or open-source tool roundups where the UI is part of the value
Tips or facts that are best understood visually rather than in pure text
Comparisons or demonstrations where seeing the interface matters
does_not_fit: Pure code walkthroughs without a visual UI — use code-content instead
Text-only tips or listicles with no visual to show — use tips-content instead
Breaking news — use news-content instead

placeholders.TITLE_LINE1: Opening segment of one editorial headline, max 18 characters. It renders together with TITLE_LINE2 as a single natural, left-aligned title block.
placeholders.TITLE_LINE2: Continuation of the same headline, max 22 characters. Do not force a separate balanced line or use generic lens labels.
placeholders.ACCENT_LINE: Purple qualifier that adds a specific practical angle, trade-off, or useful stat. Max 44 chars.
placeholders.SUBTITLE: Short supporting sentence aligned to the same left column as the title. Max 120 chars.
placeholders.IMAGE_3D_URL: AI-generated 3D render image URL — see image_3d_requirement below
placeholders.TAG: Top-right label — tool name, brand, or category. e.g. 'n8n', 'AI TOOLS', 'GITHUB'

placeholders.TITLE: Item name or step title — short, punchy. e.g. 'yt-dlp', 'Step 1: Setup', 'n8n'. Max 42 chars.
placeholders.EXPLANATION_L1: First paragraph of explanation — one substantive paragraph with a specific fact, mechanism, or implication. Max 300 chars.
placeholders.EXPLANATION_L2: Second paragraph of explanation — a substantive continuation, trade-off, or practical consequence. Max 300 chars.
placeholders.IMAGE_URL: Screenshot or visual of the tool/concept being discussed — see image_requirement below

closing.visual_note: Static CTA slide with centered typography. No image is required. Only AVATAR_URL and HANDLE are dynamic.

image_plan_guidance.description: Structured image intent for the Build AI Brief Body prompt.
image_plan_guidance.intro: Intro image is a 3D render visual (IMAGE_3D_URL). Must use assetType=3d-render with a query describing the topic rendered as a 3D dark-theme visual.
image_plan_guidance.slides: Each isi slide requires a UI screenshot, official docs screenshot, or diagram matched to that specific slide topic (IMAGE_URL). Prefer official GitHub README images or product screenshots. Never use random Unsplash images for isi slides unless no official screenshot can be found.

image_requirement.description: For content (isi) slides — find a real screenshot or visual of the tool/concept being shown.
sources: Direct screenshot URL from the tool's official GitHub README (raw image links)
Official product website screenshot or demo image
App Store / Play Store preview image if discussing a mobile app
Dashboard or UI screenshot from the tool's documentation
criteria: Must show the actual interface or visual of what is being discussed
Prefer dark-mode screenshots if available — they blend better with the dark template
Avoid images with large text overlays — the content should be clearly readable

image_3d_requirement.description: For intro slides — use an AI image generation tool to create a 3D render, OR find a high-quality 3D-style tech image.
image_3d_requirement.style: Dark background (#08080f or very dark navy), photorealistic 3D rendered objects floating in space, purple/blue glowing light, connected by thin glowing lines. Objects should represent the topic (e.g. AI chips, app icons, robotic hands, floating UI cards).
image_3d_requirement.generation_prompt_template: 3D render of [TOPIC_OBJECTS] on a dark navy background, glowing purple and blue neon light, floating connected by thin light trails, photorealistic, high detail, cinematic lighting, no text
image_3d_requirement.fallback: If image generation is unavailable, search Unsplash for: 'tech 3D render dark background purple glow' or 'AI chip holographic dark'

shared_defaults.note: The following fields are typically constant per creator — stored in a creator config profile, not generated each time.
shared_defaults.TOTAL: Always 05 for all content slide templates

template_selection_logic.description: Use this guide to select the correct template before generating content.

decision.if: Content requires displaying code, syntax, or commands
Content is tips, facts, or insights that can be split into 5 points — no code, no mandatory image
Content showcases tools, apps, CLI workflows, automations, or concepts that need screenshots, diagrams, or visual illustrations
Content is a sharp insight, claim, or reframe that doesn't need code or a visual/screenshot — including non-tech topics such as health, finance, habits, or culture
Content suits a calm, premium, editorial/lifestyle tone rather than a bold or dark treatment — no code or mandatory visual needed
Content is an energetic, urgent, hook-driven growth tip or step-by-step tactic — not a calm/premium tone
Content is triggered by a recent release, trend, model update, controversial benchmark, or industry discussion
decision.use: Select tips-content, code-content, or visual-content based on the useful angle. Never create a generic news recap.
